title: Claude Code reliability — what should we test?
_comment: Draft experiment shortlist, not implementation approval. Based on the read-only investigation of app bc9e43752, desktop CLI 2.1.302 and Android pin 2.1.300. Official references: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/{overview,events,api,reference,troubleshoot}; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance. No experiments or app edits are authorized by creating this deck. Selection scopes a later isolated test; paid runs require separate approval.

steps.intro: Choose Test this or Later for each numbered change. These are experiments, not app changes. Mods are small extensions running inside Claude Code. All tests use isolated copies; paid runs need separate approval.

steps.headline: 1. Send messages directly instead of pretending to type
steps.today: YouCoded types text and file paths into Claude Code's terminal, then sends Enter.
steps.problem: Timing and open menus can swallow a message or give Enter the wrong meaning.
steps.proposal: Try the mod's direct-send method. Pass only if long text, images and busy-session sends arrive once, without answering an open menu.

options.label: Test this
pros: Could remove paste timing and accidental menu input.
Could preserve multiline text without flattening it.
cons: Image support and queued-send confirmation are not yet proven.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the current send path while testing other changes.

steps.path: Stop · model picker · permission mode · compact
steps.headline: 2. Change conversation settings without keyboard shortcuts
steps.today: Stop, model changes and permission-mode changes send keys or commands into the terminal.
steps.problem: The app can show a change before Claude has actually applied it.
steps.proposal: Try direct mod controls. Pass only if Stop works while busy and every setting change reports its applied value or a clear refusal.

options.label: Test this
pros: Less dependence on keyboard focus.
Displayed settings could follow confirmed changes.
cons: Some controls may still need the terminal; test each separately.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep shortcut-driven controls and their existing checks.

steps.headline: 3. Answer the exact request, not its position on a menu
steps.today: Ordinary approvals use hooks; plan choices still rely on reading and answering a terminal menu.
steps.problem: A changed menu or expired request can leave a card unusable or out of date.
steps.proposal: Try addressed mod replies. Pass only if approvals, questions and every plan choice preserve their meaning through long waits, cancellation and disconnects.

options.label: Test this
pros: Could stop menu wording and layout from breaking approval cards.
Could reject stale answers instead of applying them elsewhere.
cons: Highest uncertainty: special questions, plans and mod failure may prevent full replacement.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep existing approval protections and terminal fallback; do not loosen permissions.

steps.headline: 4. Receive conversation updates directly instead of watching files
steps.today: The chat view reads Claude's changing transcript files and decodes special records for background work.
steps.problem: An upstream format change can hide replies or leave completed work spinning.
steps.proposal: Compare mod events against the existing timeline in a test session. Pass only with complete, correctly ordered replies, tool results and nested-helper activity, including reconnects.

options.label: Test this
pros: Could reduce missing updates and false completion states.
Less dependence on private transcript formatting.
cons: Events can be missed if the mod stops; history recovery still needs a separate solution.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Retain the file watcher as the live conversation source.

steps.path: Working indicator · context and usage display
steps.headline: 5. Read status directly, without watching the spinner or replacing the statusline
steps.today: Working-state checks read terminal animation; context and usage depend on files written by our statusline.
steps.problem: A terminal redesign or custom statusline can make these readings wrong or unavailable.
steps.proposal: Try mod turn and usage reports. Pass only if busy, waiting and finished states stay distinct and usage remains correct with a custom statusline.

options.label: Test this
pros: Fewer false stuck warnings.
Users could keep their own statusline without losing app statistics.
cons: A quiet model is not necessarily stuck; progress and usage coverage must be verified.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the current screen and statusline readings.

steps.page: 6–10 · Make the connection and extensions dependable
steps.intro: Select experiments independently. Any mod-based replacement also needs item 6's recovery test before adoption. Item 7 and item 9 do not require mods. No selection approves app implementation.

steps.headline: 6. Detect a broken connection before trusting it
steps.today: Several independent signals tell YouCoded what Claude is doing; a new mod would add another possible failure point.
steps.problem: Mods can be disabled or unloaded while Claude keeps running.
steps.proposal: Test a connection handshake, health checks and safe recovery. Deliberately disable or crash the test mod; pass only if unavailable actions are clear and no send or approval repeats.

options.label: Test this
pros: Makes silent integration failure visible.
A prerequisite before trusting any mod-based replacement.
cons: Users may need terminal fallback while the connection is unavailable.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Defer mod-backed replacements too; do not ship them without failure detection.

steps.headline: 7. Let Claude Code manage its own plugin installation records
steps.today: YouCoded updates four Claude Code registration files itself.
steps.problem: A partial update or changed file format can make an installed plugin invisible.
steps.proposal: Try Claude Code's official plugin commands in a disposable profile. Pass only if install, update, disable and removal survive interrupted operations and report their actual outcome.

options.label: Test this
pros: Avoids maintaining Claude's private registration formats.
Uses commands already available in the installed CLI.
cons: Scopes, offline installs and command-confirmation prompts need careful handling.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep our installer and its four-file bookkeeping.

steps.headline: 8. Show what this Claude session actually has available
steps.today: Separate file scans populate skills and commands, with a hand-maintained list of built-in commands.
steps.problem: The lists can disagree with Claude about disabled plugins, project scope or available commands.
steps.proposal: Try the mod's command list plus official plugin listings. Establish their coverage; pass only if project changes, disabled plugins and unusual install locations produce the correct available choices.

options.label: Test this
pros: Fewer commands that appear available but do not work.
Less manual upkeep when Claude adds features.
cons: No single complete discovery source is proven; some file scanning may remain.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the current scanners and built-in command list.

steps.headline: 9. Attach app tools to each session instead of rewriting shared settings
steps.today: Some tools already attach per session; other connections are copied into Claude's global configuration.
steps.problem: Concurrent updates can overwrite changes, and removed plugins can leave stale connections behind.
steps.proposal: Test per-session tool configuration while keeping the existing tool protocol. Pass only if user connections remain intact, failures are visible, and stopping a session leaves no stale app entries.

options.label: Test this
pros: Less interference with Claude used outside YouCoded.
Clearer cleanup and less persistent secret copying.
cons: App-provided tools would not automatically appear in separately launched Claude sessions.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Retain persistent projection, with concurrency and cleanup risks still to address.

steps.headline: 10. Supply app instructions without changing the user's global instructions
steps.today: YouCoded adds automatic-naming instructions to the user's global Claude instructions file.
steps.problem: App-specific instructions can affect Claude sessions launched outside YouCoded.
steps.proposal: Test session-only instructions through a mod, without redesigning naming. Pass only if YouCoded sessions receive them, unrelated sessions do not, and personal instructions remain unchanged.

options.label: Test this
pros: Cleaner separation between YouCoded and standalone Claude.
App instructions could update without editing personal files.
cons: Changing instructions too often can reduce cached reuse; disabled mods would omit these instructions.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the current global instruction section.

steps.page: 11–14 · Protect history and evaluate bigger changes
steps.intro: These cover durability, compatibility and the larger replacement option. We review test results before deciding whether to build anything. Existing subscriptions must not be silently replaced with API billing.

steps.headline: 11. Keep a durable app history separate from Claude's resume files
steps.today: YouCoded preserves copies of Claude transcripts, but still relies on their format for browsing and resume.
steps.problem: Direct mod updates alone would not recover missed events or preserve full history after a crash.
steps.proposal: Test an app-owned conversation record alongside preserved Claude resume data. Pass only if crash recovery, compaction and device transfer lose no messages and still resume correctly.

options.label: Test this
pros: Could keep readable history independent of Claude's storage changes.
Provides a recovery path for missed live updates.
cons: Large migration and extra storage; readable history is not itself a resumable Claude session.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the current durable transcript copies and handoff safeguards.

steps.headline: 12. Test each supported Claude version before calling it compatible
steps.today: Daily checks catch startup and popup changes, but many other integration behaviors are not covered that way.
steps.problem: A Claude update can still change sends, approvals, history or extension loading unnoticed.
steps.proposal: Expand checks to those behaviors and report unsupported capabilities. Pass only if deliberately changed behavior is caught on the tested desktop and Android versions.

options.label: Test this
pros: Finds breakage before users discover it.
Useful whether we adopt mods or keep today's integration.
cons: Ongoing maintenance; full checks need several operating systems and some quota-approved runs.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep the existing startup and popup checks without broader coverage.

steps.headline: 13. Make installed app hooks survive upgrades without touching unrelated hooks
steps.today: Hooks are copied to a stable folder, but write protection still points at the bundled source location.
steps.problem: Moved installations or missing scripts can leave stale commands; broad filename matching can mistake a user's hook for ours.
steps.proposal: Test stable paths, complete script checks and exact ownership in disposable installs. Pass only if relocation and missing-file repair work while similarly named user hooks stay untouched.

options.label: Test this
pros: A focused improvement that does not depend on mods.
Protects users' existing Claude customization.
cons: Does not remove the deeper limitations of hooks and terminal-driven control.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Keep current installation behavior while testing larger replacements.

steps.headline: 14. Compare the official Agent SDK with the terminal connection
steps.today: YouCoded hosts interactive Claude Code, including its terminal and subscription sign-in.
steps.problem: A mod bridge still needs custom recovery and control plumbing; the SDK provides a purpose-built app connection.
steps.proposal: Prototype an API-backed SDK session separately. Compare sends, approvals, streaming and resume; document missing terminal features, billing differences and authentication constraints before any adoption decision.

options.label: Test this
pros: The clearest documented interface for hosting Claude in another app.
Could remove most terminal-control dependence for this connection type.
cons: Not an approved drop-in subscription replacement; API usage is separately billed.
Keeping two connection types adds maintenance and terminal behavior may differ.

options.label: Later
options.summary: Focus on improvements that preserve the existing CLI and subscription arrangement.
